text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.64% today, closing a two-week slide of nearly 10%. The stock dropped on the day the company announced quarterly earnings and a leadership change, after already sliding through late October—a period when broader oil refiner concerns about guidance and forward outlook (not just past earnings) have weighed on the sector. Refinery utilization remains solid at 92.8%, but US crude oil prices are down from earlier in the month, which can compress profit margins for refiners who convert cheap raw crude into fuels.

The two-week decline fits a pattern: investors have grown cautious about Big Oil earnings season, specifically questioning what company guidance will reveal about future profitability rather than treating strong recent results as a reliable sign. A Democratic Congress (suggested as possible after the 2026 midterms) could also shift long-term energy policy toward renewables, adding uncertainty for traditional refining businesses that investors are already reassessing.
